en: The Apadāna of the Elder Raṁsisaññaka, the Sixth in the Timira Chapter I was a physician in the city of Bārāṇasī, skilled in the three branches of medical science. At that time, the Blessed One, the Teacher, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, having prepared a medicinal decoction, I went to the presence of the Buddha. Having approached him, I offered it to the Blessed One, saying: “This medicine, Blessed One, is for the sake of curing the illness of the Tathāgata. The Teacher accepted it out of compassion for me. Having accepted it, he took it and drank it. When the Blessed One had drunk it, his ailment was completely cured. Because of that deed, I rejoiced with a joyful heart. After passing away from that life, I was reborn in the world of the gods. For twenty thousand aeons, I dwelt in the realm of the Thirty-three Gods. When my lifespan there had expired, I passed away and was reborn here in the human world. I am now a forest-dwelling monk, one who lives on alms-food. My name is Raṁsisaññaka, and I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. I have reached the end of suffering; I am free from all defilements. I have no further existence; I shall not be born again. This is my final body; I shall not take up another. Thus did I perform a deed of merit toward the Tathāgata, the Fully Enlightened One. By the ripening of that karma, I have attained this state of peace. I have reached the end of suffering; I am free from all defilements. I have no further existence; I shall not be born again. Thus indeed the venerable elder Raṁsisaññaka spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Raṁsisaññaka.
